# [P2] Enforce finite numeric extraction and valid sorting in chat session exposures

## Why

`src/counter_risk/chat/session.py:700` defines `_parse_float(value)`. The function converts integers, floats, and strings without validating `math.isfinite(parsed)`. ## Why

`configure_logging` at `src/counter_risk/logging.py:38` has **zero production callers**. Its only
references anywhere in the repo are two tests: `tests/test_imports.py:15` (a `hasattr` assertion) and
`tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py:66`. The only code that installs a logging handler lives inside
that function (`src/counter_risk/logging.py:55` and `:62`).

Because nothing calls it, the root logger has no handler at runtime. Measured on an unconfigured
root logger: an `INFO` record produced empty stderr and empty stdout with `root.handlers == []`,
while a `WARNING` record reached bare stderr through `logging.lastResort`.

Call-site census in `src/`:

| level | call sites | reaches the operator |
|---|---|---|
| `debug` | 4 | no output at all |
| `info` | 33 | no output at all |
| `warning` | 27 | bare stderr, unformatted |
| `error` | 6 | bare stderr, unformatted |
| `exception` | 20 | bare stderr, unformatted |

So 37 diagnostic records in the shipped product emit nothing, and `JsonFormatter`
(`src/counter_risk/logging.py:12`) — written to make logs deterministic and auditable — never
formats a single record in production.

The missing behavior matters because the codebase deliberately degrades rather than crashing, and
records the degradation with a log call. `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:2369` reports a missing
limits config at `INFO`, which means an operator whose `config/limits.yml` is unreachable sees a
clean successful run with all limit checking silently disabled. That specific path was reproduced
during the 2026-08-24 audit: a 9,999,999,999 exposure against the shipped 250M `severity: fail`
limit returned `breach_count: 0`, `has_breaches: False`, no warnings, run completed.

This is one seam. Fixing it raises the visibility of roughly a dozen separately-filed findings.

## Scope

- `src/counter_risk/cli/__init__.py` — the entry point that must configure logging
- `src/counter_risk/logging.py` — read only; do not change its signature
- `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py` — extend with the wiring gate

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the levels of existing `LOGGER.*` calls, and do not convert any log call into a
  raise. Whether a given path should fail loudly instead of logging is decided per-path in the
  separate findings W-1, W-2 and W-3; this issue only makes the existing records observable.
- Do not add a logging framework, structured-logging library, or third-party dependency.
- Do not alter `JsonFormatter` behavior or the log-record schema.
- Do not configure logging at import time in `src/counter_risk/__init__.py` or in any library
  module. Only the CLI entry point may configure handlers.
- A scaffold-only change does NOT count as completing this issue and is a failure of this issue:
  adding the test without wiring the call, or wiring it somewhere a packaged run does not reach,
  is scaffolding rather than a fix.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a `--log-level` argument and an optional `--log-file` argument to the top-level parser in `src/counter_risk/cli/__init__.py`, defaulting the level to `INFO`.
- [ ] Call `configure_logging` once in `main` in `src/counter_risk/cli/__init__.py`, before any subcommand dispatch, passing the parsed level and log file.
- [ ] Confirm the `gui` subcommand path also reaches that call, since the packaged executable launches through it.
- [ ] Add `test_cli_main_configures_logging` to `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py`, asserting the root logger has at least one handler after `main` runs with a trivial argument list.
- [ ] Add `test_pipeline_info_records_are_emitted_after_cli_configures_logging` to `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py`, asserting an `INFO` record from the `counter_risk.pipeline.run` logger appears in captured output once the CLI has configured logging.
- [ ] Add `test_configure_logging_has_a_production_caller` to `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py`, asserting at least one non-test module under `src/counter_risk/` references `configure_logging`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py::test_configure_logging_has_a_production_caller` passes.
- [ ] `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py::test_cli_main_configures_logging` passes.
- [ ] `tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py::test_pipeline_info_records_are_emitted_after_cli_configures_logging` passes.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration.** Comment out the `configure_logging` call in `src/counter_risk/cli/__init__.py`, run `pytest tests/test_counter_risk_logging.py::test_configure_logging_has_a_production_caller` and paste the FAILING output. Restore the call, re-run the same node id, and paste the PASSING output. Both must appear in the PR body.
- [ ] Run the pipeline with an absent `config/limits.yml` and paste output showing the previously-invisible `INFO` record from `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:2369` now appearing on the operator's console.
- [ ] `ruff check .` and `black --check .` pass at the pinned versions (`ruff==0.16.4`, `black==26.5.1`).
- [ ] The full suite is no worse than the pre-change baseline of 1391 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped.

## Implementation Notes

`configure_logging` already accepts `log_level` and writes both a stream handler and an optional
JSON file handler, so no change to it is required — this is a wiring issue, not a design issue.

Configure logging exactly once, at the CLI entry point. Configuring it from a library module or at
import time would make handler installation a side effect of importing `counter_risk`, which breaks
test isolation and any host embedding the package.

Audit reference: `Code/Audits/Counter_Risk/2026-08-24-AUDIT_REPORT.md`, finding X-1 (the report's
single highest-leverage item).

body:
## Why

Two release tests decide whether PyInstaller is usable by comparing resolved interpreter
directories. `Path.resolve()` follows symlinks, and a virtualenv's `bin/python` is a symlink to the
base interpreter by default (`python -m venv`, `uv venv`), so both operands collapse to the base
interpreter's bin directory and the comparison is always equal — regardless of what is actually
installed in the active environment.

The defective guard is byte-identical at `tests/test_release_spec.py:89` and
`tests/integration/test_packaged_executable_assets.py:32`:

```python
if Path(pyinstaller).resolve().parent != Path(sys.executable).resolve().parent:
    pytest.skip("PyInstaller is not installed in the active test environment.")
```

Measured in a venv built from `requirements-dev.lock`, which does not carry `pyinstaller` (that pin
lives at `requirements.txt:11`):

```
which pyinstaller  -> a path OUTSIDE the venv
sys.executable     -> the venv python, whose resolve() lands on the base interpreter
guard says "parents differ, should skip"? -> False
is PyInstaller importable in the venv?    -> No module named 'PyInstaller'
```

So the guard reports "usable" while the import fails. Both tests then invoke a foreign PyInstaller
against the active environment's code and fail opaquely with a `CalledProcessError` naming
`release.spec` and a non-zero exit status. Nothing in that message names the real cause.

The missing behavior: the guard must key on whether `PyInstaller` is importable in the running
interpreter, which is what its own skip message already claims to test. As written, that skip
message is unreachable in the environments it was written for, and the resulting failure misdirects
exactly the person most likely to hit it — someone setting the repo up for the first time.

Remote CI is unaffected: `release-e2e.yml` installs `requirements.txt`, so `which` and importability
agree on that runner. This defect bites local developers and any environment that installs only the
dev lock.

## Scope

- `tests/test_release_spec.py`
- `tests/integration/test_packaged_executable_assets.py`
- one new test module holding the regression gate

## Non-Goals

- Adding `pyinstaller` to `requirements-dev.lock` or to the `dev` extra is out of scope. Making
  these tests *run* everywhere is a separate and larger decision; this issue is only about the guard
  reporting the truth.
- Changing what the two release tests assert once they do run is out of scope. Do not modify
  `release.spec`, `pyinstaller_runtime_hook.py`, or any workflow file.
- Deleting, skipping wholesale, or `xfail`-ing either release test to make the suite green does NOT
  count as completing this issue and is a failure of this issue.
- A scaffold-only change does NOT count as completing this issue and is a failure of this issue:
  adding the new test module without changing BOTH guard sites, or changing only one of the two
  sites, is scaffolding rather than a fix.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `import importlib.util` to `tests/test_release_spec.py`.
- [ ] Replace the resolved-parent comparison at `tests/test_release_spec.py:89` with `if importlib.util.find_spec("PyInstaller") is None:`, keeping the existing skip message unchanged.
- [ ] Add `import importlib.util` to `tests/integration/test_packaged_executable_assets.py`.
- [ ] Replace the resolved-parent comparison at `tests/integration/test_packaged_executable_assets.py:32` with the same `importlib.util.find_spec` check, keeping the existing skip message unchanged.
- [ ] Check whether `sys` is still used in each edited file and remove the import only where it has become unused.
- [ ] Create a new test module `test_pyinstaller_guard.py` under `tests/` holding the two gates below.
- [ ] Add `test_pyinstaller_guard_does_not_compare_resolved_parents`, which reads both guard files and asserts neither still contains the resolved-parent comparison, naming any offending file in the assertion message.
- [ ] Add `test_release_tests_skip_when_pyinstaller_unimportable`, which runs the release test in a subprocess with `find_spec("PyInstaller")` forced to return `None` and asserts the reported outcome is `skipped` rather than `failed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_pyinstaller_guard.py::test_pyinstaller_guard_does_not_compare_resolved_parents` passes.
- [ ] `tests/test_pyinstaller_guard.py::test_release_tests_skip_when_pyinstaller_unimportable` passes.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration.** Restore the resolved-parent comparison at `tests/test_release_spec.py:89` only, run `pytest tests/test_pyinstaller_guard.py::test_pyinstaller_guard_does_not_compare_resolved_parents`, and paste the FAILING output showing that file named as the offender. Revert the break, re-run the same node id, and paste the PASSING output. Both outputs must appear in the PR body.
- [ ] In an environment where `PyInstaller` is not importable, `pytest -rs` over both release node ids reports two SKIPPED lines with the reason `PyInstaller is not installed in the active test environment.` Paste that output.
- [ ] `ruff check .` and `black --check .` pass at the pinned versions (`ruff==0.16.4`, `black==26.5.1`).

## Implementation Notes

The fix is two lines plus two imports. It was applied and reverted during the 2026-08-24 audit; with
the change in place both release tests skip cleanly with the intended reason, instead of raising
`CalledProcessError`.

Note for whoever writes the second gate: an assertion that re-implements the defective predicate
inline and compares it against importability is a defect *detector*, not a regression gate — it

body:
## Why

`calculate_wal` in `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py:44-48` divides by a **signed** sum of row
totals, guarded only against exact zero:

```python
total_exposure = sum(row.total for row in schedule.rows)
if not math.isfinite(total_exposure):
    raise ValueError("Total exposure is not finite")
if total_exposure == 0:
    return 0.0
weighted_days = sum((row.maturity_date - px).days * row.total for row in schedule.rows)
return weighted_days / total_exposure
```

The `math.isfinite` check added by the previous audit is present and passes — a near-cancelling
denominator is perfectly finite, just close to zero. Executed against `calculate_wal` with a long
1,000,000.00 leg maturing in one year and a short 999,999.99 leg maturing in ten years:

```
signed net exposure : 0.010000000009313226
WAL (days)          : -328,799,996,041
WAL (years)         : -900,205,328
```

WAL is defined by the module docstring as an exposure-weighted average time-to-maturity in days from
the Px Date, so any correct result must fall inside the span of the schedule's own maturity dates —
here `[365, 3653]` days. The returned value is nine orders of magnitude outside it and negative.

The exact-cancellation case is worse because it is silent. A fully-hedged TIPS book sums to exactly
zero and returns `0.0`, and the docstring at `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py:14-18` declares
`0.0` to mean "there is no TIPS exposure to measure … That is the expected value for June 2026
onward, not a data error". So a hedged book and a wound-down book are indistinguishable in the
output.

Both paths reach the historical workbook through `src/counter_risk/outputs/historical_workbook.py:89`.

No existing test can catch this: `tests/test_wal.py` is 66 lines and contains no negative total, no
mixed-sign schedule, and no near-zero denominator.

## Scope

- `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py`
- `tests/test_wal.py`

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the TIPS-only selection rule or the block the parser reads. Which rows enter the
  calculation is settled and out of scope.
- Do not change the sign convention of `ExposureMaturityRow.total` or touch the parser at
  `src/counter_risk/parsers/exposure_maturity_schedule.py`.
- Do not silently substitute a magnitude denominator (`sum(abs(...))`) without recording that the
  input was mixed-sign. A wrong-but-plausible WAL is worse than a refusal, because the report has no
  other signal that the book was hedged.
- Do not widen this into a general sign-convention refactor across `compute/`. Findings C-1 and C-2
  are filed separately.
- A scaffold-only change does NOT count as completing this issue and is a failure of this issue:
  adding tests without changing the guard, or adding the guard without a distinct signal for the
  exact-cancellation case, is scaffolding rather than a fix.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py`, compute the gross magnitude `sum(abs(row.total) for row in schedule.rows)` alongside the existing signed total.
- [ ] Raise `ValueError` naming both the signed and gross totals when the gross magnitude is non-zero but the signed total is negligible relative to it, using a documented relative threshold rather than an exact-zero comparison.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py`, keep returning `0.0` only when the gross magnitude is itself zero, which is the genuine no-TIPS-exposure case the docstring describes.
- [ ] Update the module docstring in `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py` to state that `0.0` means no gross exposure, and that a hedged-to-flat book raises rather than returning zero.
- [ ] Add `test_wal_raises_on_near_cancelling_signed_denominator` to `tests/test_wal.py` using a long leg at one year and an opposing short leg at ten years.
- [ ] Add `test_wal_result_lies_within_the_schedule_maturity_span` to `tests/test_wal.py`, asserting the result falls between the earliest and latest row offsets for any schedule that returns a value.
- [ ] Add `test_wal_returns_zero_only_for_empty_gross_exposure` to `tests/test_wal.py`, distinguishing an empty schedule from an exactly-hedged one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_wal.py::test_wal_raises_on_near_cancelling_signed_denominator` passes.
- [ ] `tests/test_wal.py::test_wal_result_lies_within_the_schedule_maturity_span` passes.
- [ ] `tests/test_wal.py::test_wal_returns_zero_only_for_empty_gross_exposure` passes.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration.** Restore the bare `if total_exposure == 0: return 0.0` guard in `src/counter_risk/calculations/wal.py`, run `pytest tests/test_wal.py::test_wal_result_lies_within_the_schedule_maturity_span` and paste the FAILING output, which must show the out-of-span value and the span. Revert, re-run the same node id, and paste the PASSING output. Both must appear in the PR body.
- [ ] All pre-existing tests in `tests/test_wal.py` still pass unchanged.
- [ ] `ruff check .` and `black --check .` pass at the pinned versions (`ruff==0.16.4`, `black==26.5.1`).

## Implementation Notes

The span assertion was written and run against the current tip during the 2026-08-24 audit and fails
there with:

```
AssertionError: WAL -328,799,996,041 days is outside the span [365, 3653]
```

That is the expected pre-fix output for the deliberate-break step.

A relative threshold is the right shape here rather than an absolute epsilon, because notional
magnitudes in this book span several orders of magnitude and any fixed epsilon is either
meaningless at the top of that range or trigger-happy at the bottom.

The correct non-finite guard pattern already exists in this package at
`src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py:92`, which raises rather than returning a sentinel — worth
matching for consistency.

Audit reference: `Code/Audits/Counter_Risk/2026-08-24-01-code-quality.md` and
`Code/Audits/Counter_Risk/2026-08-24-AUDIT_REPORT.md`, finding C-3.

## Why

`_find_numeric` in `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py:121` coerces a row value with a bare
`float(raw_value)` and no finite check:

```python
try:
    return float(raw_value)
except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
    raise ValueError(f"Row value for {field!r} must be numeric") from exc
```

`float("nan")` and `float("inf")` both succeed, so a non-finite value passes straight through. The
correct guard already exists thirty lines away in the same package, at
`src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py:92`, which raises `ValueError` on non-finite input — and
`rollups.py` already imports from that module.

Downstream, `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:2101-2107` ranks counterparties with:

```python
ranked = sorted(records, key=lambda record: (-abs(_to_float(record.get(proxy_column))), ...))
```

NaN compares `False` against every value, so `sorted` cannot order it and the result depends on
input arrival order. Executed with three identical counterparty rows in three different orders, one
carrying a NaN proxy:

```
order 1 (NaN first) -> ['ALPHA BANK', 'GAMMA BANK', 'BETA BANK']
order 2 (NaN last)  -> ['GAMMA BANK', 'BETA BANK', 'ALPHA BANK']
order 3 (NaN mid)   -> ['BETA BANK', 'ALPHA BANK', 'GAMMA BANK']
control, same rows with the NaN replaced -> ['GAMMA BANK', 'BETA BANK', 'ALPHA BANK'] both orders
```

Three different answers to "which counterparty is our largest exposure", decided by row order. The
ranking is written to `risk_rankings.csv`, so a wrong and unreproducible number reaches the report.

The missing behavior is a `math.isfinite` check at the coercion boundary, matching the guard the
package already has.

No existing test can catch it: `tests/compute/test_rollups.py` is 338 lines and contains no `nan`, no `inf`,
and one negative value. The pipeline also hand-rolls the same coercion inline at
`src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:1731-1790` as `float(x or 0.0)`, where the `or 0.0` fallback is
inert because NaN is truthy.

## Scope

- `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py` — the inline coercion and the ranking sort
- `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the sign convention or the magnitude handling of any exposure metric. Findings C-2
  and C-3 are filed separately.
- Do not substitute `0.0` for a non-finite input anywhere. Coercing a NaN to zero would move the
  defect from a visibly absurd ranking to a silently wrong one, which is worse.
- Do not rewire the four unused `rollups` entrypoints in this issue. That is finding C-4 and it
  changes which code the pipeline executes.
- Do not add a sort tiebreaker as the fix. Making the sort stable would hide the bad input rather
  than reject it.
- A scaffold-only change does NOT count as completing this issue and is a failure of this issue:
  adding tests without the guard, or guarding `_find_numeric` while leaving the inline coercion in
  `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py` unguarded, is scaffolding rather than a fix.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, add a `math.isfinite` check to `_find_numeric` and raise `ValueError` naming the field and the offending value when it fails.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, confirm the `default` branch of `_find_numeric` cannot itself return a non-finite value.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py`, replace the inline `float(x or 0.0)` coercion around lines 1731-1790 with a call to the guarded helper so both paths share one rule.
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py`, make the ranking sort at lines 2101-2107 fail loudly rather than silently mis-order if a non-finite proxy value still reaches it.
- [ ] Add `test_find_numeric_rejects_nan` to `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_find_numeric_rejects_infinity` to `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_risk_ranking_is_order_independent` to `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`, ranking the same record set in three different input orders and asserting all three produce an identical ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_find_numeric_rejects_nan` passes.
- [ ] `tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_find_numeric_rejects_infinity` passes.
- [ ] `tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_risk_ranking_is_order_independent` passes.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration.** Remove the `math.isfinite` check from `_find_numeric` in `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py`, run `pytest tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_risk_ranking_is_order_independent` and paste the FAILING output showing at least two differing rankings. Restore the check, re-run the same node id, and paste the PASSING output. Both must appear in the PR body.
- [ ] All pre-existing tests in `tests/compute/test_rollups.py` still pass unchanged.
- [ ] `ruff check .` and `black --check .` pass at the pinned versions (`ruff==0.16.4`, `black==26.5.1`).

## Implementation Notes

`src/counter_risk/compute/limits.py:92` is the pattern to copy: it coerces, checks
`math.isfinite`, and raises with a message naming the constraint. Reusing that helper directly is
preferable to writing a second one, since two guards can drift.

The order-independence test is the load-bearing gate. Asserting only that `_find_numeric` rejects
NaN would pass even if a future refactor reintroduced an unguarded coercion path — the ranking
assertion pins the observable behavior the report depends on.

Audit reference: `Code/Audits/Counter_Risk/2026-08-24-01-code-quality.md` and
`Code/Audits/Counter_Risk/2026-08-24-AUDIT_REPORT.md`, finding C-1.
title: Reject non-finite values in _find_numeric so the risk ranking is deterministic

## Why

`docs/data_quality.md:28` places fallback date resolution in the `date` DQ category ("missing date header or fallback date resolution"), and `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:25` registers `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK` as `warn`-severity; `data_quality.py:50` assigns it to the `date` category. The classification logic at `data_quality.py:475–476` is already wired: any pipeline warning containing `"date derivation"` maps to `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK`. The pipeline, however, never emits such a string.

When `config.as_of_date` is `None`, `resolve_as_of_date()` (`src/counter_risk/dates.py:53–70`) falls back to CPRS workbook headers, returning a `DateResolution` with `source="cprs_header_mapping"` or `source="cprs_header_text"` (constants at `dates.py:29–30`). `run.py:412` captures `as_of_date_resolution`, but when the `warnings` list is initialized at `run.py:434`, `.source` is never inspected and no advisory is emitted. The only occurrence of `"date derivation"` in `src/` is the hard-failure `RuntimeError` at `run.py:419`, raised before `warnings` is created and never reaching `build_data_quality()`.

This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: a run that silently infers `as_of_date` from stale CPRS headers passes DQ green. Operators see a clean summary with no date advisory, with no mechanism to detect the silent fallback short of reading the manifest `date_resolution` block manually.

## Scope

- Add a fallback-source check in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py` after line 434 (`warnings: list[str] = []`): when `as_of_date_resolution.source != AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG`, append a `"date derivation fallback: ..."` warning to `warnings`.
- Extend the import at `run.py:43` to include `AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG` from `counter_risk.dates` (currently only `resolve_as_of_date` and `resolve_run_date` are imported).
- Add a unit test in `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py` that passes the new warning string through `ManifestBuilder.build()` and asserts the `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK` finding has `category="date"` and `severity="warn"`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the hard-failure behavior when `resolve_as_of_date()` raises `ValueError`; the `RuntimeError` at `run.py:419` stays as-is.
- Do not add operator UI changes to Runner.xlsm or the Tk runner — the fix only wires the warning into the existing DQ pipeline.
- Do not change the manifest `date_resolution` block; it already records `source` correctly.
- Do not add directional baseline checks or touch the concentration-metrics baseline kit.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding an import or warning string without asserting `code="DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK"`, `category="date"`, `severity="warn"` from a real `build_data_quality()` call is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:43`, extend the import from `counter_risk.dates` to also include `AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG` (currently only `resolve_as_of_date` and `resolve_run_date` are imported).
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py`, after `warnings: list[str] = []` at line 434, add: if `as_of_date_resolution.source != AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG`, append `f"date derivation fallback: as_of_date inferred from workbook headers (source={as_of_date_resolution.source})"` to `warnings`.
- [ ] Confirm the new warning string contains `"date derivation"` to satisfy the existing check at `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:475` without any modification to `data_quality.py`.
- [ ] In `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py`, add `test_manifest_build_date_resolution_fallback_produces_warn_finding` following the fixture pattern at lines 24–57: pass `warnings=["date derivation fallback: as_of_date inferred from workbook headers (source=cprs_header_mapping)"]` to `ManifestBuilder.build()` and assert `code="DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK"`, `category="date"`, `severity="warn"` in `manifest["data_quality"]["findings"]`.
- [ ] Add `test_manifest_build_date_resolution_fallback_absent_when_config_provides_date` in the same file: pass no `"date derivation"` warning and assert `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK` is absent from findings.
- [ ] Run `pytest tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py -v` and confirm all five tests pass (three existing plus two new).
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture the FAIL output, then revert before requesting review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py::test_manifest_build_date_resolution_fallback_produces_warn_finding` passes with findings containing `code="DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK"`, `category="date"`, `severity="warn"`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily change the new warning string in `run.py` so it omits `"date derivation"` (e.g., rename to `"as_of_date fallback:"`). Running `pytest tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py::test_manifest_build_date_resolution_fallback_produces_warn_finding` **must FAIL** — the finding is no longer classified as `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK`. Revert and confirm the test passes again. Capture both outputs in the PR.
- [ ] All three pre-existing tests in `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py` pass without modification (`test_manifest_build_populates_data_quality_from_warnings`, `test_manifest_build_data_quality_defaults_to_info_when_no_warnings`, `test_manifest_build_collects_data_quality_from_validation_context`).
- [ ] `rg "date derivation" src/` from the repo root returns exactly two hits: the new warning-append in `run.py` and the existing `RuntimeError` at `run.py:419`.
- [ ] PR cites `docs/data_quality.md:28` as the design source defining the `date` category and the `DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK` contract.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:43` — current import from `counter_risk.dates`; add `AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG` here.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:410–419` — date derivation try-block; `as_of_date_resolution` captured at line 412, `.source` never checked for warnings.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:434` — `warnings: list[str] = []`; insert the fallback source check immediately after.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:419` — existing `RuntimeError` for date derivation failure; do not touch.
- `src/counter_risk/dates.py:28–30` — `AS_OF_SOURCE_CONFIG = "config"`, `AS_OF_SOURCE_HEADER_MAPPING = "cprs_header_mapping"`, `AS_OF_SOURCE_HEADER_TEXT = "cprs_header_text"`.
- `src/counter_risk/dates.py:53–70` — `resolve_as_of_date()` returning `DateResolution` with `.source` set to one of the three constants above.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:25` — `"DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK": "warn"` in `_SEVERITY_BY_CODE`.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:50` — `"DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK": "date"` in `_CATEGORY_BY_CODE`.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:471–476` — `_code_from_message` dead branch: `"date derivation" in message_lower → "DATE_RESOLUTION_FALLBACK"`.
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/manifest.py` — `ManifestBuilder.build()` accepts `warnings` list; follow the call signature at `test_manifest_data_quality.py:35–46`.
- `tests/pipeline/test_manifest_data_quality.py:24–57` — existing fixture pattern to copy for the two new tests.
- `docs/data_quality.md:28` — design source; cite in PR description.

## Why

`docs/operator_ux_decision.md` (lines 147–154, "Output Folder Convention and Naming") specifies that standard operator runs land in `runs/<as_of_date>` (e.g., `runs/2026-01-31`) and same-date repeat runs append a numeric suffix (`runs/2026-01-31_1`). The pipeline's `_create_run_directory` implements this contract: `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:165–169` confirms first run lands in `runs/2026-02-13`, second run in `runs/2026-02-13_1`. When `--output-dir` is supplied and the directory is non-empty, the pipeline raises `FileExistsError` (`tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:231–240`).

`src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115` hard-codes `_000000`: `f"{resolve_output_root(repo_root, output_root)}\\{parsed_date.isoformat()}_000000"`. `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:72` repeats the same literal: `output_root / f"{month_end.isoformat()}_000000"`. Both always pass `--output-dir runs/<date>_000000` to the pipeline, bypassing automatic naming entirely. On a second same-month operator run, the pipeline receives a non-empty `_000000` directory and raises `FileExistsError` — the repeat-run protection the pipeline provides can never trigger because the launcher never omits `--output-dir`.

This is **latent fragility becoming a guaranteed crash** on any same-month re-run: the first run succeeds; the second fails with `FileExistsError` rather than landing in `runs/<date>_1`. Post-run helpers (`Open Output Folder`, `Open Manifest`, `Open Summary`, `Open PPT Folder`) in both VBA and Python also resolve the `_000000` hard-coded path, so after a corrected run they would open a directory that does not exist.

## Scope

- Remove the `_000000` hard-coded suffix from `resolve_output_dir` in `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py` and `_resolve_output_dir` in `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py`; either omit `--output-dir` (letting the pipeline's automatic naming run) or implement a shared suffix-safe resolver that mirrors `_create_run_directory` logic.
- Align `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas` `ResolveOutputDir` with the chosen strategy so VBA and Python agree on what folder name a given operator run produces.
- Update all post-run open-folder helpers in VBA and Python (`OpenOutputFolder_Click`, `OpenSummary_Click`, `OpenManifest_Click`, `OpenPPTFolder_Click`, and their Python counterparts) so they resolve the actual generated run directory.
- Update `docs/operator_ux_decision.md`, `docs/gui_runner.md`, and `docs/macro_spec.md` to remove the `_000000` convention and describe the repeat-run-safe naming contract.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redesign the full release packaging or remote trigger flow.
- Do not change the manifest schema or generated report contents except for the recorded output path if needed.
- Do not route workflow-template or agent-lane maintenance into this repo.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: changing the resolver in `runner_launch.py` while leaving `_000000` in `gui/runner.py`, or updating docs without fixing all callers, is a failure. All three launcher surfaces (VBA, `runner_launch.py`, `gui/runner.py`) must agree on the same non-`_000000` contract.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115`, remove the `_000000` literal from `resolve_output_dir`. Either omit `--output-dir` from `build_command` so the pipeline's automatic naming runs, or implement a suffix-safe resolver that reads existing run-folder count and returns the correct next name (matching `_create_run_directory` in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py`).
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:72`, update `_resolve_output_dir` to use the same strategy, removing `f"{month_end.isoformat()}_000000"`. The fix automatically propagates to `_resolve_ppt_output_dir` (line 76), `_open_output`, `_open_manifest`, `_open_summary`, and `_open_ppt` callbacks.
- [ ] In `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:226–234`, update `ResolveOutputDir` so it no longer formats a date-only value with `RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT = "yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss"` and passes the result as `--output-dir`; align with the Python resolution strategy.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_gui_runner.py:78` (asserts `result.output_dir == Path(tmp_path / "runs" / "2025-12-31_000000")`) and `tests/test_gui_runner.py:348` (asserts `opened_paths == [Path("runs/2025-12-31_000000")]`) to reflect the corrected behavior. Add a test confirming two same-`as_of_date` operator runs do not resolve to the same fixed output directory.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_runner_xlsm_vba_project.py::test_runnerlaunch_bas_contains_required_behavior_markers` (lines 33–49) if VBA marker assertions reference the old `yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss` convention in a way that must change.
- [ ] Update `docs/operator_ux_decision.md` lines 147–154 ("Output Folder Convention and Naming"), `docs/gui_runner.md` "Launch" section, and `docs/macro_spec.md` `MS-OPEN-OUTPUT` spec to remove references to `_000000` and document the repeat-run-safe naming contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py::test_run_directory_creation_same_date_repeat_run_uses_unique_directory_suffix` passes unchanged, confirming the pipeline's own repeat-run contract is unbroken.
- [ ] A new test in `tests/test_gui_runner.py` (e.g., `test_execute_gui_run_same_date_does_not_produce_fixed_000000_path`) asserts that the `output_dir` field from `execute_gui_run` is no longer a `_000000`-suffixed path.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily restore `_000000` in `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115` (revert to `f"{parsed_date.isoformat()}_000000"`). The new repeat-run test above must FAIL with the reverted code, confirming the new test would catch the regression. Revert after capturing the failure.
- [ ] `tests/test_gui_runner.py::test_execute_gui_run_builds_run_args_and_writes_settings` passes with the updated output-dir assertion (no longer `_000000`).
- [ ] `rg "_000000" src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py` returns no matches, confirming the hard-coded suffix is fully removed from both Python callers.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_runner_xlsm_vba_project.py::test_runnerlaunch_bas_contains_required_behavior_markers` passes with the updated VBA.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:111–115` — `resolve_output_dir`; `_000000` literal on line 115; the comment on line 113 explicitly acknowledges VBA's midnight-time behavior produces deterministic `_000000`.
- `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:69–72` — `_resolve_output_dir`; `_000000` literal on line 72.
- `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:75–76` — `_resolve_ppt_output_dir` delegates to `_resolve_output_dir`; fix propagates automatically.
- `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:8` — `RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT As String = "yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss"`; line 233 — `Format$(parsedDate, RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT)` applied to a date-only value (midnight → `_000000`).
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py` — contains `_create_run_directory`; the authoritative suffix-safe logic; study before implementing the resolver so both agree.
- `tests/test_gui_runner.py:78` — asserts `result.output_dir == Path(tmp_path / "runs" / "2025-12-31_000000")`; must be updated.
- `tests/test_gui_runner.py:348` — asserts `opened_paths == [Path("runs/2025-12-31_000000")]`; must be updated.
- `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:114–173` — authoritative same-date repeat-run test; do not modify, use as acceptance reference.
- `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:231–240` — `test_create_run_directory_with_non_empty_output_dir_raises`; confirms the pipeline guard that makes `_000000` on repeat a `FileExistsError`.
- `docs/operator_ux_decision.md:147–154` — "Output Folder Convention and Naming" section; design source of truth.
title: Align Runner and GUI output folders with the pipeline repeat-run contract

## Why

`docs/concentration_metrics.md` (CSV columns section) commits to deterministic per-`(variant, segment)` output for all segments including TIPS, Treasury, Equity, Commodity, Currency, Cash, and `total`. `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:33–38` includes treasury (cp_a=120, cp_b=50, cp_c=30; total=200) and equity (cp_a=70, cp_b=30; total=100) in the base exposure table, so both segments produce real metric values on every run.

However, `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:80–123` contains only six directional entries, all targeting `all_programs.total.*` metrics (`hhi`, `top5_share`, `top10_share`). `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:129–132` lists only those three `total`-segment keys as `priority_metrics`. `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md:3–4` records 33.3% coverage (3 of 9 parameters exercised, 6 unexercised). Treasury and equity segment metrics (`all_programs.treasury.hhi`, `all_programs.equity.hhi`, etc.) are computed and emitted on every pipeline run but have no enforced directional invariant.

This is **latent fragility**: a regression in treasury metric computation (e.g., wrong normalization that halves all HHI values) would produce a false-direction result the current suite cannot detect. `tests/baseline/test_invariants.py` checks mathematical bounds (range `[0,1]`, `top5_le_top10`, HHI floor) but does not verify that a specific perturbation moves treasury or equity HHI in the economically correct direction.

## Scope

- Add treasury-segment and equity-segment scenarios to `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` using the `set_notional` patch op to concentrate mass onto cp_a in each segment.
- Add directional entries with `enforce: true` targeting at least `all_programs.treasury.hhi` and `all_programs.equity.hhi`.
- Extend `priority_metrics` in `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` to include the two new keys.
- Regenerate `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md` to show ≥55% coverage.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add directional checks for TIPS, Commodity, Currency, or Cash segments — the base scenario only includes treasury and equity as non-total segments, so there is no base data to perturb for those.
- Do not modify `compute_concentration_metrics` or add new pipeline features.
- Do not add golden master tests — directional checks are the appropriate harness for this surface.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding scenarios and directional entries with `enforce: false`, or adding them without extending `priority_metrics`, is a failure of this issue. `test_priority_metrics_covered` must pass and the deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` under `scenarios`, add a `treasury_concentrated` scenario with patch `{op: set_notional, segment: treasury, counterparty: cp_a, value: 1000.0}` to concentrate all treasury mass on cp_a (base treasury HHI ≈ 0.445; concentrated value approaches 1.0).
- [ ] In `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` under `scenarios`, add an `equity_concentrated` scenario with patch `{op: set_notional, segment: equity, counterparty: cp_a, value: 900.0}` to concentrate equity mass on cp_a (base equity HHI ≈ 0.58; concentrated value approaches 1.0).
- [ ] In `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` under `directionals`, add `{id: treasury_concentrated_raises_hhi, scenario: treasury_concentrated, control: base, metric: all_programs.treasury.hhi, direction: increase, enforce: true}`.
- [ ] In `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` under `directionals`, add `{id: equity_concentrated_raises_hhi, scenario: equity_concentrated, control: base, metric: all_programs.equity.hhi, direction: increase, enforce: true}`.
- [ ] Extend `priority_metrics` in `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` to include `all_programs.treasury.hhi` and `all_programs.equity.hhi`.
- [ ] Run `BASELINE_REFRESH_REPORT=1 pytest tests/baseline/test_coverage_manifest.py::test_emit_coverage_report` to regenerate `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md` and confirm it shows ≥55% coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/baseline/test_directional.py` passes with at least two new parametrized cases (`treasury_concentrated_raises_hhi` and `equity_concentrated_raises_hhi`), both enforced, confirming the correct directional response to concentration patches on non-total segments.
- [ ] `tests/baseline/test_coverage_manifest.py::test_priority_metrics_covered` passes after `priority_metrics` in `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` includes `all_programs.treasury.hhi` and `all_programs.equity.hhi`.
- [ ] `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md` shows ≥55% coverage (at least 5 of 9 parameters exercised) after running `BASELINE_REFRESH_REPORT=1 pytest tests/baseline/test_coverage_manifest.py::test_emit_coverage_report`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily change `direction: increase` to `direction: decrease` on the `treasury_concentrated_raises_hhi` entry in `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml`. The `test_directional[treasury_concentrated_raises_hhi]` parametrized case must FAIL with "Economically wrong direction". Revert after capturing the failure, confirming the check enforces real economics rather than scaffolding.
- [ ] `rg "enforce: true" tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` returns at least 8 matches (6 existing + 2 new), confirming both new directional entries are enforced.

## Implementation Notes

- `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:23–38` — base exposure table; treasury segment on lines 33–35 (cp_a=120, cp_b=50, cp_c=30), equity on lines 37–38 (cp_a=70, cp_b=30). Hand-calculated base values: treasury HHI ≈ (120/200)²+(50/200)²+(30/200)² = 0.445; equity HHI ≈ (70/100)²+(30/100)² = 0.58.
- `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:44–74` — existing scenarios; new entries append here.
- `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:80–123` — existing directionals (all `total`); new entries append after line 123.
- `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:129–132` — `priority_metrics` list; extend with two new keys.
- `tests/baseline/adapter.py` — contains `run_scenario` and the patch DSL; verify `set_notional` is a supported `op` before writing the new scenarios (it is used in the `more_concentrated` and `single_entity` scenarios on lines 50–68).
- `tests/baseline/test_directional.py:25–38` — parametrized harness; picks up new catalog entries automatically via `load_catalog(CATALOG_PATH)`.
- `tests/baseline/test_coverage_manifest.py:48–52` — `test_priority_metrics_covered`; asserts `m.priority_gaps == set()`.
- `tests/baseline/test_coverage_manifest.py:55–63` — `test_emit_coverage_report`; run with `BASELINE_REFRESH_REPORT=1` to update `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md`.
- `docs/reports/baseline-coverage.md:3` — current state: 3 of 9 (33.3%); target ≥5 of 9 (≥55.6%).
- `docs/concentration_metrics.md` (CSV columns section) — design source confirming per-segment deterministic output contract for Treasury and Equity.
title: Add directional baseline checks for treasury and equity concentration metric segments

## Why

`docs/operator_ux_decision.md` (lines 147–154, "Output Folder Convention and Naming") specifies that standard operator runs land in `runs/<as_of_date>` (e.g., `runs/2026-01-31`) and same-date repeat runs append a numeric suffix (`runs/2026-01-31_1`). The pipeline's `_create_run_directory` implements this contract: `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:165–169` confirms first run lands in `runs/2026-02-13`, second run in `runs/2026-02-13_1`. When `--output-dir` is supplied and the directory is non-empty, the pipeline raises `FileExistsError` (`tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:231–240`).

`src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115` hard-codes `_000000`: `f"{resolve_output_root(repo_root, output_root)}\\{parsed_date.isoformat()}_000000"`. `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:72` repeats the same literal: `output_root / f"{month_end.isoformat()}_000000"`. Both always pass `--output-dir runs/<date>_000000` to the pipeline, bypassing automatic naming entirely. On a second same-month operator run, the pipeline receives a non-empty `_000000` directory and raises `FileExistsError` — the repeat-run protection the pipeline provides can never trigger because the launcher never omits `--output-dir`.

This is **latent fragility becoming a guaranteed crash** on any same-month re-run: the first run succeeds; the second fails with `FileExistsError` rather than landing in `runs/<date>_1`. Post-run helpers (`Open Output Folder`, `Open Manifest`, `Open Summary`, `Open PPT Folder`) in both VBA and Python also resolve the `_000000` hard-coded path, so after a corrected run they would open a directory that does not exist.

## Scope

- Remove the `_000000` hard-coded suffix from `resolve_output_dir` in `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py` and `_resolve_output_dir` in `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py`; either omit `--output-dir` (letting the pipeline's automatic naming run) or implement a shared suffix-safe resolver that mirrors `_create_run_directory` logic.
- Align `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas` `ResolveOutputDir` with the chosen strategy so VBA and Python agree on what folder name a given operator run produces.
- Update all post-run open-folder helpers in VBA and Python (`OpenOutputFolder_Click`, `OpenSummary_Click`, `OpenManifest_Click`, `OpenPPTFolder_Click`, and their Python counterparts) so they resolve the actual generated run directory.
- Update `docs/operator_ux_decision.md`, `docs/gui_runner.md`, and `docs/macro_spec.md` to remove the `_000000` convention and describe the repeat-run-safe naming contract.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redesign the full release packaging or remote trigger flow.
- Do not change the manifest schema or generated report contents except for the recorded output path if needed.
- Do not route workflow-template or agent-lane maintenance into this repo.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: changing the resolver in `runner_launch.py` while leaving `_000000` in `gui/runner.py`, or updating docs without fixing all callers, is a failure. All three launcher surfaces (VBA, `runner_launch.py`, `gui/runner.py`) must agree on the same non-`_000000` contract.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115`, remove the `_000000` literal from `resolve_output_dir`. Either omit `--output-dir` from `build_command` so the pipeline's automatic naming runs, or implement a suffix-safe resolver that reads existing run-folder count and returns the correct next name (matching `_create_run_directory` in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py`).
- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:72`, update `_resolve_output_dir` to use the same strategy, removing `f"{month_end.isoformat()}_000000"`. The fix automatically propagates to `_resolve_ppt_output_dir` (line 76), `_open_output`, `_open_manifest`, `_open_summary`, and `_open_ppt` callbacks.
- [ ] In `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:226–234`, update `ResolveOutputDir` so it no longer formats a date-only value with `RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT = "yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss"` and passes the result as `--output-dir`; align with the Python resolution strategy.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_gui_runner.py:78` (asserts `result.output_dir == Path(tmp_path / "runs" / "2025-12-31_000000")`) and `tests/test_gui_runner.py:348` (asserts `opened_paths == [Path("runs/2025-12-31_000000")]`) to reflect the corrected behavior. Add a test confirming two same-`as_of_date` operator runs do not resolve to the same fixed output directory.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_runner_xlsm_vba_project.py::test_runnerlaunch_bas_contains_required_behavior_markers` (lines 33–49) if VBA marker assertions reference the old `yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss` convention in a way that must change.
- [ ] Update `docs/operator_ux_decision.md` lines 147–154 ("Output Folder Convention and Naming"), `docs/gui_runner.md` "Launch" section, and `docs/macro_spec.md` `MS-OPEN-OUTPUT` spec to remove references to `_000000` and document the repeat-run-safe naming contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py::test_run_directory_creation_same_date_repeat_run_uses_unique_directory_suffix` passes unchanged, confirming the pipeline's own repeat-run contract is unbroken.
- [ ] A new test in `tests/test_gui_runner.py` (e.g., `test_execute_gui_run_same_date_does_not_produce_fixed_000000_path`) asserts that the `output_dir` field from `execute_gui_run` is no longer a `_000000`-suffixed path.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily restore `_000000` in `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:115` (revert to `f"{parsed_date.isoformat()}_000000"`). The new repeat-run test above must FAIL with the reverted code, confirming the new test would catch the regression. Revert after capturing the failure.
- [ ] `tests/test_gui_runner.py::test_execute_gui_run_builds_run_args_and_writes_settings` passes with the updated output-dir assertion (no longer `_000000`).
- [ ] `rg "_000000" src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py` returns no matches, confirming the hard-coded suffix is fully removed from both Python callers.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_runner_xlsm_vba_project.py::test_runnerlaunch_bas_contains_required_behavior_markers` passes with the updated VBA.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:111–115` — `resolve_output_dir`; `_000000` literal on line 115; the comment on line 113 explicitly acknowledges VBA's midnight-time behavior produces deterministic `_000000`.
- `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:69–72` — `_resolve_output_dir`; `_000000` literal on line 72.
- `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:75–76` — `_resolve_ppt_output_dir` delegates to `_resolve_output_dir`; fix propagates automatically.
- `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:8` — `RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT As String = "yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss"`; line 233 — `Format$(parsedDate, RUN_FOLDER_FORMAT)` applied to a date-only value (midnight → `_000000`).
- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py` — contains `_create_run_directory`; the authoritative suffix-safe logic; study before implementing the resolver so both agree.
- `tests/test_gui_runner.py:78` — asserts `result.output_dir == Path(tmp_path / "runs" / "2025-12-31_000000")`; must be updated.
- `tests/test_gui_runner.py:348` — asserts `opened_paths == [Path("runs/2025-12-31_000000")]`; must be updated.
- `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:114–173` — authoritative same-date repeat-run test; do not modify, use as acceptance reference.
- `tests/test_pipeline_run_dir.py:231–240` — `test_create_run_directory_with_non_empty_output_dir_raises`; confirms the pipeline guard that makes `_000000` on repeat a `FileExistsError`.
- `docs/operator_ux_decision.md:147–154` — "Output Folder Convention and Naming" section; design source of truth.
title: Align Runner and GUI output folders with the pipeline repeat-run contract

**Why.** Numeric facts a downstream Style-Drift & Exposure Monitor will read — `top_exposures` (built at `run.py:1599`, emitted at `manifest.py:106`), `concentration_metrics`, `risk_rankings` — are emitted as bare value dicts with no back-pointer to their source cell/row, file, or extraction method, and parsed data carries no confidence (grep for `class Evidence|source_id|excerpt` in `src/` → none; `confidence` exists only for PPT shape matching at `run.py:3105-3133`). Parsers already know the source location internally: NISA tracks `header_row` and per-sheet header columns (`_select_worksheet_and_headers`, `src/counter_risk/parsers/nisa.py:221-232`) and repo-cash sources enumerate `row_index` (`src/counter_risk/parsers/repo_cash_sources.py:47,249`) — but discard it from outputs. Without an evidence back-pointer, a consumer cannot trace a counterparty exposure number to its source or assess trust.

**Scope.** Introduce a lightweight, typed `Evidence` record and thread it onto ONE high-value output to start: `top_exposures`. `source_id` reuses the existing `input_hashes` key namespace (`run.py:586-588`) so evidence ties to an already-hashed source. Persist in the manifest and extend the schema.

**Non-Goals.**
- Full excerpt capture for every cell, retrofitting every parser, or PDF OCR confidence modeling.
- Threading evidence onto `concentration_metrics`/`risk_rankings` in this issue (follow-up once the pattern is proven on `top_exposures`).
- Scaffold-only is disallowed: defining an `Evidence` dataclass that is never populated, or attaching an `evidence` field whose `source_id` does NOT correspond to a real `input_hashes` key, does NOT satisfy this issue.
- Privacy boundary: this work runs entirely in the deterministic core on real workbook data (permitted). It must NOT widen what the LangSmith export emits — `langsmith_fleet.SENSITIVE_FIELD_TOKENS` already strips `counterparty`/`exposure`/`notional`/`prompt`/`completion` (`langsmith_fleet.py:63-68`); the new `evidence`/`source_id` fields must stay inside the local `manifest.json` and not be added to any exported/LLM-bound payload.

**Tasks.**
- [ ] Define an `Evidence` TypedDict/dataclass (`source_id: str`, `sheet: str | None`, `row: int | None`, `method: str`, `confidence: float | None`) in a new module e.g. `src/counter_risk/pipeline/evidence.py` (or beside `parsing_types.py`).
- [ ] Capture source location in the NISA parse path feeding exposures: surface the `header_row`/sheet already computed in `_select_worksheet_and_headers` (`nisa.py:221`) and the data `row_index` so the exposure builder can attach it.
- [ ] In the exposure builder (`run.py:1582-1626`), attach an `evidence` field to each `top_exposures[variant]` entry with `source_id` set to the matching `input_hashes` key (the variant's source workbook), `sheet`, `row`, and `method="nisa_parser"`.
- [ ] Extend `manifest_schema()` `top_exposures` typing to allow the nested `evidence` object (currently `{"type": "object"}` at `manifest_schema.py:189`; tighten to describe per-entry `evidence`), and document the evidence field in `README.md`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**
- [ ] Concrete failing-then-passing test (in `tests/pipeline/`, exercising the exposure builder or a fixture run): asserts at least one `top_exposures` entry has `entry["evidence"]["source_id"]` that is a key present in `manifest["input_hashes"]`, and a non-null `entry["evidence"]["row"]` and `entry["evidence"]["sheet"]`. FAILS on current `main` (no `evidence` field).
- [ ] The evidence-bearing manifest passes `validate_manifest` (schema-enforcement issue).
- [ ] A test asserts the LangSmith fleet export for the same run does NOT contain `source_id`/`evidence` (confirm the strip boundary at `langsmith_fleet.py:63-68` is not bypassed).

**Implementation Notes.** Reuse `input_hashes` keys as the `source_id` namespace — they are computed from `_resolve_input_paths` (`run.py:586-588`). Start narrow (`top_exposures` only) to keep the diff reviewable. The exposure construction is `top_exposures[variant] = [...]` at `run.py:1599`; the NISA header/row knowledge to plumb is at `nisa.py:221-232`. This issue depends on the schema-enforcement issue for the new key to survive `additionalProperties: False`.

**Why.** Warnings are emitted as structured records — `WarningsCollector.warn`/`add_structured` produce dicts with `row_idx`, `message`, optional `code`, and filtered extras (`src/counter_risk/pipeline/warnings.py:44-67`). The `data_quality.findings` path consumes that structure (`_build_warning_findings` reads `warning.get("message")`/`warning.get("code")`, `data_quality.py:129-148`). But the manifest's top-level `warnings` array **flattens every record to a single human string** via `_normalize_warning` (`manifest.py:400-421`, e.g. `"message (code=X, row_idx=7)"`), and the schema types it as `array of string` (`manifest_schema.py:191`). Consumers reading `manifest["warnings"]` lose the machine-readable `code`, the `row_idx`, and any source pointer — the only place a raw warning links to *where* it came from. The collector already proves the structure exists (`tests/test_warnings_collector.py:8-77`), but no test asserts that structure survives into the written manifest.

**Scope.** Emit warnings in the manifest as structured objects preserving `code`, `row_idx`, and source extras, while keeping a rendered human string per entry for backward compatibility and `DATA_QUALITY_SUMMARY.txt`. Update the schema accordingly.

**Non-Goals.**
- Building the full Evidence object (separate issue below) — this issue only preserves the fields the collector ALREADY captures.
- Changing `data_quality` (already structured).
- Scaffold-only is disallowed: adding a `warnings_structured` key to the schema without populating it from the real collector records, or dropping the existing rendered-string form (breaking the summary renderer), does NOT satisfy this issue.

**Tasks.**
- [ ] In `ManifestBuilder.build` (`manifest.py:97-120`), add a `warnings_structured` array built from the raw `warnings` argument (the collector dicts), preserving `code`, `row_idx`, `message`, and any retained extras; keep the existing `warnings` string array (`_normalize_warnings`, `manifest.py:392-398`) unchanged for backward compatibility.
- [ ] Add a `_normalize_warning_structured(warning)` helper alongside `_normalize_warning` (`manifest.py:400-421`) that returns the dict form (dropping only `None`/blank values, mirroring `_is_blank_warning_value` semantics from `warnings.py:8-14`) or `None` for empty entries.
- [ ] Add `warnings_structured` to `manifest_schema()` `properties` as an array of objects requiring `message` (string) and allowing `code`/`row_idx`/additional keys; leave it OUT of `required` for backward compatibility, OR add to `required` only if the schema-enforcement issue lands first.
- [ ] Add manifest-propagation assertions to `tests/test_warnings_collector.py` (or a new `tests/pipeline/` test): feed a `WarningsCollector` with `warn("invalid row", code="MISSING_DESCRIPTION", row_idx="12", description="TY Mar25")`, pass `collector.warnings` into `ManifestBuilder.build(... warnings=...)`, write, reload the JSON, and assert the structured fields are present as discrete keys.

**Acceptance Criteria.**
- [ ] Concrete failing-then-passing test: asserts the written `manifest.json` has a `warnings_structured` entry where `entry["code"] == "MISSING_DESCRIPTION"`, `entry["row_idx"] == 12`, and `entry["description"] == "TY Mar25"` as DISCRETE fields (not substring-embedded in a string). This FAILS on current `main` (no such key).
- [ ] The legacy `warnings` string array is unchanged: an existing-style assertion that `manifest["warnings"]` still contains the rendered `"... (code=MISSING_DESCRIPTION, ...)"` form still passes, and `_build_data_quality_summary` (`manifest.py:208-326`) renders without error.
- [ ] The structured form passes `validate_manifest` (schema-enforcement issue) when present.

**Implementation Notes.** `data_quality.py:129-148` already shows the structured→finding conversion; mirror that read-fidelity for the raw `warnings` array. The collector's public `warnings` property returns copies of dicts (`warnings.py:69-72`), so the structured source is already available at the `build()` call site (`run.py:603` passes `warnings=warnings`). Verify whether `warnings` reaching `build()` is the collector dicts or a pre-flattened list at the `run.py:603` call site and thread the dicts through if needed.

body:
**Why.** The manifest captures input hashes (`run.py:586-588` via `_sha256_file`) and a full config snapshot (`manifest.py:380-390`), but omits the producing tool's version, git SHA, and Python/platform — so a replayed or compared run cannot be tied to the exact code that produced it. There is also no `manifest_schema_version` on the manifest to evolve the contract safely, even though the sibling LangSmith fleet record already carries a `schema_version` (`src/counter_risk/observability/langsmith_fleet.py`). Agent-ready checklist item 6 (provenance) is currently only Partial for exactly this reason. This blocks reproducible audit and safe cross-repo contract versioning.

**Scope.** Add (1) a top-level `manifest_schema_version` string and (2) a `provenance` object (`tool`, `tool_version`, `git_sha`, `python_version`, `platform`) to `ManifestBuilder.build` and to `manifest_schema()`. Populate side-effect-free.

**Non-Goals.**
- Per-artifact output-file hashing (out of scope; inputs already hashed).
- Evidence-object/cell-level provenance (separate issue below).
- Scaffold-only is disallowed: adding the keys to the schema without populating real values in `build()`, or hardcoding a placeholder `git_sha="unknown"` unconditionally instead of a best-effort lookup, does NOT satisfy this issue.

**Why** The pipeline's deterministic compute/IO core is fully working and headless-capable — `run_pipeline_with_config(config, *, config_dir, output_dir, formatting_profile)` (`src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:261`) is a clean in-process entry that produces `manifest.json` + `DATA_QUALITY_SUMMARY.txt` (`src/counter_risk/pipeline/manifest.py:21,139`) and emits only **relative** output paths (asserted in `tests/pipeline/test_run_pipeline.py::test_run_pipeline_writes_expected_outputs_and_manifest`, the `not Path(output_path).is_absolute()` loop ~line 1834). But a non-developer evaluator on a locked-down work PC (no installs, no terminal, browser only) or a home Mac has **no** way to try it: there is no web app (no Streamlit/Flask/FastAPI/Gradio in `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, or code), no `.devcontainer`, no hosted demo, and no CI artifact that surfaces a run folder — the only `upload-artifact` steps are agent/metrics/release (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `agents-weekly-metrics.yml`, etc.), and `release.yml` builds a Windows-only PyInstaller `.exe` only on release. The README itself frames the operator path as an Excel/Windows-app Runner (`README.md:7`), not a browser.

**Privacy constraint (binding on this issue):** the org cannot send proprietary counterparty data to external/community SaaS (no Streamlit Community Cloud, no public Hugging Face Space with real data) and cannot send proprietary data to external LLMs without authorization. It has no objection to deterministic programs processing real data. Therefore the browser demo MUST be one of: (a) **client-side WebAssembly** (stlite/Pyodide/JupyterLite) running entirely in the evaluator's browser with zero data egress; (b) **internal browser-accessible hosting** inside the org perimeter (internal web app / Posit Connect / Streamlit-in-Snowflake / internal Azure app); or (c) an **external demo using only the bundled synthetic fixtures** in `tests/fixtures/`. In every case the LLM chat surface (`src/counter_risk/chat/`) must be DISABLED or gated behind an authorized no-train endpoint — the demo must never call an external LLM with uploaded data.

**Scope** Deliver the lowest-effort viable browser path that meets the constraint, plus a smoke test. Recommended: (1) a `workflow_dispatch` CI job that runs the fixture pipeline and uploads the run folder as a viewable artifact (synthetic-fixture-only, zero real data), AND (2) a thin stlite/Pyodide single-page app committed under `web/` that loads the bundled fixtures and renders the data-quality summary + manifest entirely client-side, with the chat feature compiled out. Pick at least the CI artifact path as the floor; the stlite page is the higher-value add.

**Non-Goals**
- Do NOT deploy any app or CI demo that ingests, uploads, or transmits real/proprietary counterparty data to an external service — fixtures only for any externally reachable surface.
- Do NOT wire the LangChain chat assistant (`src/counter_risk/chat/session.py`, `chat/providers/langchain_runtime.py`) into the public/browser demo; it must be disabled or stubbed (the offline stub gate `COUNTER_RISK_CHAT_OFFLINE_MODE=1` exists for exactly this).
- Do NOT add browser-path documentation to the README `## Testing` section — `tests/test_readme_testing_section.py` asserts that section is exactly one autopilot-smoke sentence of 10-20 words and will fail; document the demo in `WORKFLOW_USER_GUIDE.md` or a new `docs/browser_demo.md` instead.
- A committed scaffold (empty `web/` dir, a workflow that does not actually upload a run folder) does NOT close this; the artifact must be downloadable/openable and the smoke test must run the fixture pipeline.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Add a `workflow_dispatch`-triggered job (new `.github/workflows/demo-artifact.yml`, or a gated job in `ci.yml`) that installs deps, runs the fixture pipeline via `python -m counter_risk.cli run --fixture-replay --config config/fixture_replay.yml --output-dir runs/demo`, and `actions/upload-artifact`s the resulting `runs/demo/` folder (manifest.json, DATA_QUALITY_SUMMARY.txt, the historical xlsx, the two PPTX, any CSVs).

Parent coordination issue: stranske/Workflows#2150

## Why

Counter_Risk already has chat trace correlation, but the monthly risk/report workflows need richer run-level metadata and a repo-specific LangSmith project to make optimization practical. The repo's core outputs include data-quality summaries, concentration metrics, risk proxy outputs, and limit breaches; LangSmith collection should make those workflow outcomes traceable without exposing sensitive counterparty data.

## Scope

- Default LangSmith to a Counter Risk specific project name.
- Preserve existing chat trace correlation.
- Add tracing and dashboard metadata for risk/report workflow runs.
- Correlate trace records with data-quality, concentration, risk proxy, and limit-monitoring outputs.
- Emit dashboard-compatible `langsmith-fleet/v1` NDJSON records for traced risk workflows.
- Keep no-secret behavior clean in local and CI runs.

## Non-Goals

- Do not log raw counterparty positions, confidential exposure records, or full report payloads into dashboard artifacts.
- Do not alter deterministic risk calculations except to add observability side effects.
- Do not make LangSmith required for monthly package generation.

## Performance Questions

This work should make it possible to answer:

- Which risk/report steps fail, fallback, or produce incomplete output?
- How often do data-quality problems drive poor or missing risk outputs?
- Which scenarios or as-of dates correlate with limit breaches or high severity summaries?
- How do model/provider choices affect generated explanations or report assistance?
- Which runs have complete trace coverage across chat and risk/report workflows?

## Tasks

- [ ] Confirm and set the default LangSmith project name for Counter_Risk.
- [ ] Preserve existing chat trace IDs/URLs and correlation behavior.
- [ ] Add workflow spans or trace events for data-quality summary, concentration metrics, risk proxy outputs, limit monitoring, report generation, and related chat/explanation calls where applicable.
- [ ] Add shared metadata for run ID, as-of date, scenario, provider, model, status, trace ID/URL, latency, and error category.
- [ ] Add domain metadata for data-quality status, concentration metric availability, risk proxy status, limit breach count/severity, and report artifact references where available.
- [ ] Emit dashboard-compatible `langsmith-fleet/v1` NDJSON records with shared fields plus Counter_Risk domain metadata.
- [ ] Add fixtures or tests for successful workflow trace records, error/fallback records, project selection, and no-secret fallback.
- [ ] Update docs/runbooks that explain how chat and risk workflow traces should be inspected together.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Counter_Risk uses a repo-specific LangSmith project by default.
- [ ] Chat trace correlation remains intact.
- [ ] Risk/report workflow traces include run, as-of date, scenario, limit, provider/model, status, trace ID/URL, and error metadata.
- [ ] Dashboard records validate against the Workflows fleet contract from stranske/Workflows#2150.
- [ ] Dashboard artifacts use hashes or artifact references instead of raw sensitive exposure/report data.
- [ ] Tests cover project selection, trace metadata, dashboard record emission, and no-secret fallback.
- [ ] Documentation identifies which workflow artifacts can be correlated with trace records.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant local anchors from the prior evaluation include:

- `README.md`
- `docs/data_quality.md`
- `docs/concentration_metrics.md`
- `docs/risk_proxy_outputs.md`
- `docs/limit_monitoring.md`
- `docs/chat_logging.md`

Use the existing deterministic report output contracts as the source for domain metadata. The Workflows parent issue owns the shared schema and dashboard ingestion; this issue owns Counter_Risk-specific collection and domain fields.

- Run focused chat/risk/report tests touched by the change.
- Run the new LangSmith metadata/dashboard artifact tests.

## Why

`README.md:10-15` says the monthly package produces updated PowerPoint files plus optional distribution PPT/PDF deliverables in the run folder, and `docs/operator_ux_decision.md:43-46` tells operators to use `Open PPT Folder` for post-run review. Current main still routes that action to `<run_dir>/distribution_static`: `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:21` and `:129-130`, `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:15` and `:245-247`, and `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:262-264` all embed that subdirectory. The pipeline writes the canonical PowerPoint artifacts directly under `run_dir`: `src/counter_risk/pipeline/ppt_naming.py:34-41` resolves the Master/Distribution filenames, `_write_outputs` creates/appends them at `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:2015-2155`, and `ManifestBuilder` records them through `output_paths`/`ppt_outputs` at `src/counter_risk/pipeline/manifest.py:95-125`. Operators can therefore click the intended review button after a successful PPT-enabled run and land in a missing folder while the registered PPTs exist one level up.

## Scope

- Align `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py` and `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas` so Excel Runner opens the run location that actually contains the registered PPT deliverables.
- Align `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py` so Tkinter `Open PPT Folder` uses the same resolved target instead of constructing `distribution_static` inline.
- Update `docs/gui_runner.md`, `docs/operator_ux_decision.md`, and `docs/remote_trigger_testing.md` to describe the same PPT retrieval location exposed by manifest/readme output metadata.
- Add regression coverage that fails if normal PPT retrieval is wired back to an uncreated `distribution_static` folder.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the canonical Master/Distribution filename rules in `src/counter_risk/pipeline/ppt_naming.py`.
- Do not implement static chart image rendering, PDF fallback behavior, or Office COM availability changes.
- Do not redesign run-folder naming, selected-date parsing, or output-root selection.
- Do not change reconciliation, limit-breach, or data-quality severity semantics.
- Do not change `manifest.json` schema fields beyond relying on existing `output_paths` and `ppt_outputs`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the `_PPT_OUTPUT_DIRNAME = "distribution_static"` path contract in `src/counter_risk/runner_launch.py:21`/`:129-130` with a resolver for the selected run folder or another manifest-backed directory containing the canonical PPT files.
- [ ] Mirror that behavior in `assets/vba/RunnerLaunch.bas:15`, `OpenPPTFolder_Click`, and `ResolvePPTOutputDir` so macro and Python parity tests agree.
- [ ] Update `src/counter_risk/gui/runner.py:250-264` so `Open PPT Folder` opens the shared PPT-output target.
- [ ] Revise `docs/remote_trigger_testing.md:98-108`, `docs/gui_runner.md:38-45`, and `docs/operator_ux_decision.md:43-46`/`:146-155` to remove `distribution_static/` as the retrieval contract unless that directory is actually created and registered.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_runner_launch.py:216-233` and missing-directory coverage so `open_ppt_output_folder` succeeds for the documented PPT parent path and reports that path on failure.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_gui_runner.py` with a headless/stub assertion that the `Open PPT Folder` button opens the same target as the Excel Runner helper.
- [ ] Keep `tests/test_pipeline_run_outputs.py:91-99`, `tests/pipeline/test_monthly_pipeline_ppt_outputs.py:99-129`, and `tests/pipeline/test_run_folder_readme.py:106-134` passing so the produced PPTs remain registered in manifest/readme output metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_runner_launch.py tests/test_gui_runner.py` passes and proves Runner open-path helpers no longer expect `<run_dir>/distribution_static` for normal PPT-enabled retrieval.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_pipeline_run_outputs.py tests/pipeline/test_monthly_pipeline_ppt_outputs.py tests/pipeline/test_run_folder_readme.py` passes, proving Master/Distribution PPT files remain created in `run_dir` and registered in manifest/readme output metadata.

- [ ] Missing-output errors still include the exact attempted path and no longer mention `distribution_static` unless that is the real registered location.

Relevant files:
- `README.md` - high-level output contract.
- `docs/gui_runner.md` - GUI button inventory.

- `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run_folder_outputs.py` - run-folder README text.
